name: mitram
description: A standalone AI coding agent with chat and tool use.

commands.title: M.I.T.R.A.M: Copy Diagnostics for Bug Report

mitram.endpoint.description: Azure AI Foundry endpoint for Claude, e.g. https://<resource>.services.ai.azure.com/anthropic/. Read from user settings only, so a repository cannot send your API key elsewhere.

mitram.model.description: Model or deployment name on your Foundry resource.

mitram.openai.endpoint.markdownDescription: An OpenAI-compatible endpoint for GPT and other non-Claude models: your Azure OpenAI resource, such as `https://<resource>.openai.azure.com/`, or a base URL such as `https://api.openai.com/v1`. The models in `mitram.openai.models` are sent here; if `mitram.endpoint` is empty, every model is. Must use https unless it is on this machine. Read from user settings only, so a repository cannot send your API key elsewhere. Set the key with **M.I.T.R.A.M: Set OpenAI API Key**.

mitram.openai.models.markdownDescription: Models served by `mitram.openai.endpoint`: on Azure OpenAI, your deployment names, such as `gpt-5.6-sol`. They appear in the model picker, and choosing one sends the chat to that endpoint.

mitram.openai.apiVersion.markdownDescription: The `api-version` sent to an Azure OpenAI resource. Not used with an `/openai/v1` URL or with other OpenAI-compatible servers.

mitram.maxIterations.description: Maximum model/tool steps for one message. When reached, the agent pauses and offers a Continue button.

mitram.skipApprovalPrompts.markdownDescription: Skip approval prompts for file edits, file creation and commands. Commands blocked by M.I.T.R.A.M's safety policy remain blocked. Read from user settings only. Off by default.

mitram.autoApproveEdits.markdownDescription: Apply `edit_file` and `create_file` without asking. Use **Revert changes** to undo a turn. Off by default.

mitram.autoApproveSafeCommands.markdownDescription: Run a tiny set of read-only commands (`pwd`, `ls`, `git status/diff/log/show`) without asking. Every other command always asks. Off by default.

mitram.blockedCommandPatterns.markdownDescription: Extra regular expressions. A command matching any of them is blocked without asking, e.g. `terraform\\s+destroy`.

mitram.contextWindow.description: Your model deployment's context window in tokens. Older context is trimmed when the conversation passes about 70% of it.

mitram.promptCaching.description: Cache the system prompt, tools and conversation prefix to cut cost and latency. Turn this off if your deployment rejects cache_control.

mitram.includeEnvironment.description: Send open tabs, the git branch and diff summary, and current errors with each message.

mitram.retrieveContext.description: Before each message, search the workspace locally for code related to it and attach the best matches: a short list of files and line ranges, and excerpts from the top two. Adds up to about 1,400 tokens, and only when the match is confident.

mitram.autoApproveCommands.markdownDescription: Commands that run without asking in every workspace. Each entry is a regular expression that must match the **whole** command, e.g. `npm test`, `python3? hello\\.py` or `npm run (lint|build)`. Commands containing `;`, `&`, `|`, `>`, `<`, backticks or `$(` always ask, and blocked commands stay blocked. For one project, choose **Always allow** on a command's approval card instead, and review those with `/permissions`. Only user settings count here, so a repository cannot set this.

mitram.models.description: Extra model or deployment names to offer in the model picker (the /model command or the model chip above the composer).

mitram.showReasoning.description: Show the model's reasoning summary while it works. If your deployment doesn't support it, M.I.T.R.A.M falls back automatically.

mitram.collapseToolCalls.description: Fold the agent's tool calls and reasoning between two replies into one line, such as "Read 3 files, ran 2 commands". It shows what is running while the agent works and folds away when it is done. Approval prompts always stay visible. Click the line to see every step.

mitram.maxRunMinutes.description: Pause a run after this many minutes (0 for no limit). A Continue button resumes it.

mitram.verifyBeforeDone.description: Before finishing, make the agent check files it changed (run tests, build or linter) and finish the tasks on its board. It is reminded at most twice.

mitram.summarizeContext.description: When a long conversation nears the context limit, replace the oldest part with a short model-written summary instead of dropping it. Uses one extra model request.

mitram.subagents.markdownDescription: Let the agent hand self-contained tasks to sub-agents that work in parallel, each with its own context, and report back. Sub-agents follow the same approval settings and safety rules, and in plan mode they can only read.

mitram.maxConcurrentRuns.markdownDescription: How many chats may have the agent working at the same time. A chat keeps working when you start a new one or switch to another; past this number, a chat waits for another to finish. Each one makes its own model requests and shares your deployment's rate limit.

mitram.maxParallelSubagents.markdownDescription: How many sub-agents may work at the same time; more wait their turn. Each one makes its own model requests, so a higher number finishes sooner but uses your deployment's rate limit faster.

command.description: Local server: the executable to run, e.g. "npx".

env.description: Environment variables for the server process. Use ${env:NAME} to take a value from your own environment.

url.description: Remote server endpoint. Must use https, unless it points at localhost.

headers.description: Extra HTTP headers for a remote server.

transport.description: Usually inferred: "stdio" for a command, "sse" for a URL ending in /sse, "http" otherwise.

auth.description: How this server's API key is sent. The key itself is kept in VS Code's secret storage, never here.

kind.description: Send the key as an HTTP header (remote) or an environment variable (local), or "oauth" to sign in through your browser (remote servers only; no name or key needed).

name.description: The header or variable name, e.g. "Authorization" or "GITHUB_TOKEN".

format.description: Template for the value, with {key} standing for the secret, e.g. "Bearer {key}".

enabled.description: Turn this server off without removing it.

mitram.mcpServers.markdownDescription: MCP servers whose tools the agent may use, as a map of name to settings. Manage these from the **MCP servers** panel in the chat view, or edit them here. API keys are stored in VS Code's secret storage, never in this file. Read from user settings only, so a repository cannot make M.I.T.R.A.M start a process.

mitram.blockedMcpTools.markdownDescription: Regular expressions matched against full MCP tool names (`mcp__<server>__<tool>`). A matching tool is blocked without asking, e.g. `mcp__.*__delete_.*`.

mitram.autoApproveMcpReads.markdownDescription: Run MCP tools the server marks as read-only without asking. The hint comes from the server itself, so leave this off unless you trust every server you have configured. Off by default.

enumDescriptions: Desktop notification when VS Code is not in front, for an approval request, a finished run, a pause or an error. A VS Code message if the window is in front but the chat is hidden.
Always raise a desktop notification, even while you are looking at the chat.
mitram.notifications.markdownDescription: When to show an operating system notification, so you know the agent needs you while you are in another window. Works on Windows, macOS and Linux (Linux needs `notify-send`). The text is the action's one-line summary, e.g. `Run npm test`. When VS Code runs on a remote machine, VS Code messages are used instead.

enumDescriptions: Your browser's own speech recognition (Chrome, Edge or Safari). Nothing to set up, but the browser vendor's service hears the audio.
Record in the browser and send the audio to the transcription endpoint below (OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Groq, or a local Whisper server). Works in any browser.
mitram.voice.provider.description: How speech is turned into text for voice prompts. Audio never goes through VS Code's webview, which cannot use a microphone: a small page opens in your browser to listen.

mitram.voice.endpoint.markdownDescription: OpenAI-compatible transcription endpoint, used when `mitram.voice.provider` is `endpoint`: a full URL such as `https://api.openai.com/v1/audio/transcriptions`, or a base URL such as `http://localhost:8000/v1`. Must use https unless it is on this machine. Read from user settings only, so a repository cannot send your audio elsewhere. Set the key with **M.I.T.R.A.M: Set Voice API Key**.

mitram.voice.model.description: Transcription model, or the deployment name on Azure OpenAI.

mitram.voice.compactWindow.description: Open the voice page as a small window with no tabs or address bar, when Chrome, Edge, Brave or Chromium is installed. Otherwise, or when off, it opens in your default browser.

mitram.voice.language.markdownDescription: Language to listen for, such as `en-US` (browser) or `en` (endpoint). Empty uses the browser's language.

mitram.mcpToolLimit.markdownDescription: Largest number of MCP tools offered to the model at once. Tool definitions cost tokens on every request, so extra tools beyond this are dropped and listed in the log.

scripts.build: npm run build:ext && npm run build:ui
scripts.build:prod: node esbuild.js --production && npm --prefix webview-ui run build
